name: WA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: DelBene's overwhelming financial advantage ($3.5M raised vs ~$3K)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: DelBene holds a D+15 district with a massive fundraising edge and no serious outside spending against her, while markets price her near certain to win. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpectedly strong Republican outside spending would be the only plausible route to tightening this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Suzan DelBene, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Seattle-area district that leans Democratic by about fifteen points. She advanced to the general election and faces Republican Mary Silva, a first-time candidate with minimal resources.

The financial picture is lopsided: DelBene has raised roughly $3.5 million and holds over $1 million on hand, while Silva has raised about $3,000. No outside groups are opposing DelBene, and prediction markets give her roughly a 97% chance of winning. With no public polling and no expert ratings flagging the race, everything points to a safe Democratic hold with a margin in the low twenties.
